items.stem: Why is random k-fold cross-validation inappropriate for evaluating a forecasting model on time-ordered data?

options.text: It lets future observations leak into training, inflating apparent accuracy
options.rationale: Correct: shuffling allows future points into training, which leaks information and overstates accuracy.

options.text: It is always slower than other methods
options.rationale: Speed is not the core issue; validity is.

options.text: It cannot compute any error metric
options.rationale: Error metrics can still be computed; the problem is leakage.

options.text: It requires the data to be stationary first
options.rationale: Stationarity is a modeling concern, not the reason k-fold leaks.

items.explanation: Correct: shuffling allows future points into training, which leaks information and overstates accuracy.

items.stem: Which method is well suited to a series with both trend and strong seasonality?

options.rationale: Correct: Holt-Winters models level, trend and seasonality together.
A global mean ignores both trend and seasonality.
Random sampling does not forecast a time series.
Dropping seasonality discards the structure you need to model.

items.explanation: Correct: Holt-Winters models level, trend and seasonality together.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when reporting a business forecast? (Select TWO)

options.text: Include prediction intervals, not just a point estimate
options.rationale: Correct: intervals communicate the uncertainty around the estimate.

options.text: State the assumptions and the forecast horizon
options.rationale: Correct: assumptions and horizon let the audience judge the forecast.

options.text: Present the forecast as a certainty
options.rationale: Forecasts are uncertain; presenting certainty misleads.

options.text: Hide the historical error from the audience
options.rationale: Hiding historical error prevents honest assessment of reliability.

items.explanation: Correct: intervals communicate the uncertainty around the estimate.; Correct: assumptions and horizon let the audience judge the forecast.
